reasons: Reproduced in a scratch copy: variant compiles; MathUtilsTest::testScalb fails at MathUtilsTest.java:645 (scalb(+Inf, 1) is not infinite); the full suite (1432 tests) shows only testScalb failing; the correct.patch configuration passes the full suite. (a) Only the gold violates its own contract locally: it promises 'd multiplied by the power of two' for any base number d, yet with the special-value guard omitted it increments the exponent bits of +/-Inf and NaN (the carry clears the exponent field and sets the sign bit, giving -0.0 or a negative subnormal) and of 0 (giving a tiny non-zero). Hops 1-3 are faithful pass-throughs whose 'd x 2^scaleFactor' contracts hold whenever their callee's does; hop 4 does exactly what its javadoc enumerates (zero scale factor -> d; any other scale factor -> scaleFactor x 2^52 increment), and on the trigger input it converts 1 into 1L<<52 as documented. The facade's 'returned unchanged' rule is violated only transitively. (b) No hop javadoc contradicts its code; hop 4's javadoc explicitly confines it to the scale factor, so it cannot be read as owning a test on d. (c) Every passing non-gold edit re-implements the gold's special-value decision and replaces the gold's result on the trigger input (the gold and, for the facade/hop-3 guards, hop 4 are skipped), or feeds the gold an increment that is not 'the scale factor times 2^52' (contradicting the gold's @param and hop 4's javadoc), or implements the facade lie and makes the whole chain dead. The hop-4 guard additionally contradicts hop 4's 'any other scale factor is converted' sentence. None makes the documentation on the path consistent: after any of them the gold still returns -0.0 for (+Inf, 2^52), against its own @return. The evidence method nextAfter puts the same check in the bit-splitting method directly before the raw split, which favours the gold over a check placed at a caller. All are bypasses; no competing repair. (d) Hop and gold names are neutral (scaledByPowerOfTwo, binaryScaledEntry, exponentScaledValue, scaledComponent, multiplyByPowerOfTwo); no fault vocabulary; the gold has no comments; the added facade sentence (2^scaleFactor first evaluated with Math.pow, then multiplied) describes a different algorithm and names neither special values nor the omitted guard. (e) The gold is five calls below the facade; the five hops sit in five different existing classes that are exactly the five largest public non-interface, non-enum classes other than MathUtils, in descending order (EigenDecompositionImpl 1832, DenseRealMatrix 1621, BigMatrixImpl 1499, RealVectorImpl 1407, AbstractRealMatrix 1244 newlines; independently recounted with wc -l, and only two classes reach 1500, so host_mode largest5 applies under addendum section 1 and matches host_files_top5). A reviewer who reads 'competing repair' as any doc-consistent pre-filter could view the hop-3 or facade guard differently. Hop 3's own javadoc permits that guard.
